h1: The 7 Best Laptop Cooling Pads for ASUS Laptops of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cooling Pads for ASUS: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 7 best laptop cooling pads for ASUS ROG, TUF, ZenBook and VivoBook laptops, matched by size, noise and airflow.
mainKeyword: laptop cooling pads for ASUS laptops
summary: The Razer Adaptive Smart pad is the best overall, with a 140mm fan up to 3000 RPM, magnetic frames for 14 to 18 inch laptops and automatic control. The llano V12 is the heavy-duty pick for big ROG and TUF machines. The ChillCore covers the largest ROGs cheaply, while the TECKNET 12 to 15.6 inch pad suits VivoBooks quietly.
intro: ASUS builds everything from a thin 14 inch ZenBook to an 18 inch ROG, so the first cooling pad mistake is shopping for the wrong end of that range. A 15.6 to 19 inch turbo pad swallows a VivoBook, and a 12 to 15.6 inch pad leaves a big ROG hanging off the edges with its intake vents uncovered. Match the pad to the chassis before you look at fan counts, because airflow that misses the vents does nothing.

Our editors reviewed seven pads from their listings and ranked them on fit range, fan design, noise, adjustability and warranty. A cooling pad helps a laptop breathe, but it does not fix dust inside the case, which we flag where it matters.

products.name: Razer Laptop Cooling Pad Adaptive Smart, Intelligent Fan Control
products.verdict: Automatic fan control and swappable frames for the premium ROG or TUF buyer.
products.description:
The Razer pad pairs a 140mm brushless fan, capable of up to 3000 RPM, with an airtight foam-sealed pressure chamber. The seal matters because it forces air through the laptop's intake vents, instead of letting it escape around the sides. Three interchangeable magnetic frames cover 14 to 18 inch laptops, and a 3-port USB Type A hub passes ports back.

It ranks first because those frames cover most ASUS gaming sizes with one pad, and fan control is automatic. Against the llano V12 it costs more, in the $100 to $200 bucket, but it adds a 2-year warranty.

Buy it for a ROG or TUF owner who wants set-and-forget cooling. The honest caveat is RPM: the fan tops out at 3000, below some rivals, and it is the most expensive pad in the guide.
products.idealFor: ROG and TUF owners wanting automatic fan control.
products.skipIf: You want the cheapest active cooling.

products.name: llano V12 Gaming Laptop Cooling Pad Laptop Cooler Laptop Cooling Fan Stand
products.verdict: A turbo fan and reinforced chassis for big, heavy ASUS gaming laptops.
products.description:
The llano V12 targets sustained airflow under a big, heavy chassis. A 5.5 inch turbo booster fan runs on a 36W power output, a removable dust filter keeps the intake clean, and a reinforced chassis holds laptops from 15.6 to 19 inches without flexing. It sells in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It ranks second because it concentrates airflow at a price well under the Razer, but gives up automatic control and a stated warranty. Concentrated air helps most when a large gaming laptop runs hot for hours.

Buy it for a large ROG or TUF under heavy loads. Skip it for anything smaller than 15.6 inches, because the pad would overhang. Its 3-port hub is only USB 2.0, so do not plan to run external drives through it.
products.idealFor: Large ROG or TUF laptops under heavy loads.
products.skipIf: Your ASUS is smaller than 15.6 inches.

products.name: ChillCore Laptop Cooling Pad, RGB Lights 9 Fans for 15.6-19.3 Inch Laptops
products.verdict: Broad airflow coverage for the largest ASUS laptops on a small budget.
products.description:
The ChillCore uses nine fans across top and bottom vents for laptops from 15.6 to 19.3 inches. An LCD shows fan speed, eight heights tilt the keyboard, ten RGB modes add lights and two USB ports pass through. At $25 to $50, it covers the biggest ROG models at the lowest cost.

It ranks third because the airflow is spread across nine smaller fans instead of one strong one like the llano. That makes it gentle and broad rather than forceful.

Buy it for a 17 to 19 inch ROG on a tight budget. The caveats are that spread airflow struggles against a single hot GPU area, and the RGB lighting adds little cooling value. Treat it as a good stand with extra airflow, not a replacement for the llano's concentrated blast.
products.idealFor: 17 to 19 inch ROG models on a budget.
products.skipIf: You have a smaller ASUS laptop.

products.name: TECKNET Laptop Cooling Pad with Phone Stand, 12-15.6 Inch
products.verdict: A quiet, right-sized pad for thinner ASUS laptops.
products.description:
The TECKNET 12 to 15.6 inch pad has nine fans at up to 2600 RPM, a rated noise level under 40 dB and five height settings up to 6 inches. A built-in phone holder and two USB ports round it out. At $25 to $50, it is sized properly for thinner ASUS laptops.

It ranks fourth because it is the right size and the quietest pad here for a VivoBook, but it will not suit large ROG laptops. It also offers modest cooling power compared with the turbo-fan designs above.

It suits students and office users who want a calm desk. The caveat is scale: a 17 inch laptop will overhang it. If you own a ZenBook or VivoBook, this is the pad that actually fits.
products.idealFor: VivoBook owners wanting a quiet, right-sized pad.
products.skipIf: You own a 17 inch or larger ASUS.

products.name: Kootek Laptop Cooling Pad Cooler Stand with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17 Inch Laptop
products.verdict: Run one fan for light work or all five for heavy tasks.
products.description:
The Kootek has five fans, one large and four small, with two switches that let you run one fan, or all five. That makes it flexible: light office work needs one quiet fan, while a heavy day can use the full set. It fits laptops from 12 to 17 inches, has six height settings and a dual USB hub, and costs under $25.

It ranks fifth because the listing gives no RPM or noise figure, so you cannot judge its power. Against the TECKNET it covers more sizes, but its numbers are unstated.

Choose it for a ZenBook that alternates light and heavy days. The caveat: without a documented RPM, trust the switches rather than a number, and expect modest cooling. Its blue LEDs are cosmetic.
products.idealFor: ZenBook owners with light and heavy work days.

products.name: ICE COOREL Gaming Laptop Cooling Pad 15-17.3 Inch, 6 RGB Cooling Fans, LCD Screen
products.verdict: Active cooling for a TUF laptop with a tight budget.
products.description:
The ICE COOREL has six transparent fans, an LCD showing fan speed, six height settings, seven RGB modes, two USB ports and a phone stand, fitting laptops from 15 to 17.3 inches. It targets gamers who want a lit-up desk without spending much, at $25 to $50.

It ranks sixth because six fans spread the airflow instead of concentrating it, so it trails the llano on heavy loads. The feature list leans toward lighting and display, not cooling power.

It suits TUF owners who want active cooling on a budget. Skip it if your laptop throttles under heavy load, because a stronger single fan will do more. If cooling is the priority, the llano V12 costs a little more and delivers noticeably more air.
products.idealFor: TUF owners wanting active cooling on a budget.
products.skipIf: Your laptop throttles under heavy load.

products.name: TECKNET Laptop Cooling Pad, Portable Slim Laptop Cooler for 12-17 Inch Laptops
products.verdict: A thin, packable pad for ZenBook and VivoBook travel.
products.description:
The slim TECKNET has three fans at 1200 RPM, a thin portable profile, a 12 to 17 inch fit and USB power. It folds into a bag, which makes it the traveller's pad, and it costs $25 to $50.

It ranks last because three fans at 1200 RPM move the least air in the guide. In exchange it takes almost no space when packed.

Buy it for light travel use with a ZenBook or VivoBook, where the goal is a cooler lap and a better typing angle. The caveat is that it is modest for gaming loads. A ROG running a heavy game will outrun it, so do not expect it to hold turbo clocks.
products.idealFor: Travelers with a ZenBook or VivoBook.

whatMatters.detail: Pads state a laptop size range in inches, such as 12 to 15.6 or 15.6 to 19. If your laptop is outside it, the pad wobbles or leaves part of the base uncovered. Check your screen size against the stated range before ordering, and consider the intake vent location on your model, which sits underneath on most ASUS laptops.

whatMatters.factor: One big fan versus many small fans
whatMatters.detail: A single turbo fan pushes concentrated air at the hottest area, while arrays of small fans spread a gentler flow. Concentrated air helps under heavy gaming loads, while quiet multi-fan pads are enough for office work. Decide which workload you have, then look at the fan layout in the listing rather than the fan count alone.

RPM is how fast a fan spins, and higher usually means louder. A pad rated under 40 dB is hard to hear, while a high-RPM fan can be intrusive in a quiet room. Look for stated RPM and decibel figures, and avoid pads that list neither, because you cannot predict their noise or airflow from the photos.

Raising the back of the laptop changes typing comfort and airflow, since a gap under the case lets cool air in. More settings let you find a comfortable angle. Check the number of heights and the maximum lift on the listing. Several pads here offer five or six heights, and the ChillCore offers eight.

Pads usually draw power from a laptop USB port, which takes a port you may need. A built-in hub passes some ports back, but the hub may be USB 2.0 and slow. Count the ports and check the version if you plan to plug in a mouse, headset or drive. A powered fan can also drain a battery.

faq.q: Will a cooling pad fit my ASUS laptop?
faq.a: Check the stated size range against your screen size. Most pads cover 15.6 to 17 inches, while ultrabooks need the 12 to 15.6 inch TECKNET. Large ROG models may need the ChillCore or llano for 19 inch coverage, and bigger laptops need a firmer base.

faq.q: What is the biggest cooling pad mistake?
faq.a: Buying a pad too big or too small for the laptop. Poor fit leaves vents uncovered and wastes airflow. Match the listed range first, then compare fans and noise. A well-fitted cheap pad beats a mismatched premium one.

faq.q: Is the Razer pad worth it over the llano V12?
faq.a: If you want automatic control and a 2-year warranty, yes. The llano delivers strong airflow for less money. The Razer wins on convenience and frame options, but costs noticeably more, and its fan tops out at 3000 RPM.

faq.q: How do I set up a pad?
faq.a: Plug it into a USB port, place the laptop so the intake vents sit over the fans, and pick a height. Start on low speed and increase only under load, to keep noise down and let the laptop reach a steady temperature first.

faq.q: How do I maintain a cooling pad?
faq.a: Wipe dust off the fans and grille every month or two. The llano V12 has a removable filter to simplify this. Dust builds up and cuts airflow, which cancels the pad's benefit if you let it build.

faq.q: Can a pad stop thermal throttling?
faq.a: It can help, but it does not replace cleaning the internal fans or repasting the processor. Treat it as a supplement, because severe throttling often points to dust or dried paste, which a pad cannot cure.

finalTake: Buy the Razer if you own a ROG or TUF and want fan control handled for you. Choose the llano V12 for sustained airflow under big loads, the ChillCore for a 17 to 19 inch laptop on a budget, and the TECKNET or Kootek for ZenBooks and VivoBooks. The slim TECKNET is for travel only.
